bull.b: AI inference workloads and KV-cache requirements are creating a structural increase in NAND demand, while data-center growth is already outpacing the broader market. This expands SanDisk’s addressable opportunity and supports sustained revenue growth over the next several quarters.

Very high margins and cash conversion provide substantial internal funding for technology development, capacity needs, and shareholder returns. The debt-free balance sheet also reduces financial risk and gives SanDisk flexibility to manage the memory cycle or pursue strategic opportunities.

Growing non-binding memorandum coverage improves demand visibility and indicates that customers are seeking dependable future NAND allocations. A pipeline exceeding supply through the decade could support utilization, planning discipline, and more durable revenue than purely spot-driven sales.

bear.b: The recent earnings improvement is powerful but has not yet demonstrated consistency across a full cycle. The sharp reversal from losses to unusually high margins and profits raises the risk that future results could normalize materially if memory conditions or mix benefits weaken.

Consumer weakness shows that pricing actions can pressure demand in a branded business even when the company retains broad distribution and user reach. Continued contraction would reduce diversification and place greater dependence on enterprise, data-center, and AI-related growth.

The current product mix and long wafer-production cycle limit SanDisk’s ability to quickly align output with customer demand. Persistent allocation constraints could defer shipments, restrict revenue capture, and make execution more dependent on forward planning over the next several quarters.
